extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, third-party submitters, and USPTO examiners/staff
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and content rules for submitting prior art under 37 CFR 1.501 and for requesting ex parte reexamination under 35 U.S.C. 302/37 CFR 1.510, including required elements, service, filing mechanics, representation, and handling by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission qualifies for entry under 37 CFR 1.501
rubrics_metrics.description: A submission under 37 CFR 1.501 must be limited to patents, printed publications, and/or patent owner written claim scope statements and additional information and include the requisite citation description and information and proof of service on the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: May be submitted via mail, hand-delivery, or the USPTO patent electronic filing system if properly filed as a 1.501 prior art submission (not as a follow-on paper). Submissions under 1.501 cannot be filed for design or plant patents. Both registered and unregistered users may make an electronic submission. Submitting papers directly into the patent by someone other than the patent owner’s representative may violate the Office's electronic filing agreement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office forwarding and Technology Center review
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions under 37 CFR 1.501 received in the Office will be forwarded to the Technology Center that currently examines the technology where the patent is classified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Technology Center is responsible to promptly determine whether the submission meets statute and rule requirements and to enter it into the patent file at the appropriate time if proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling submissions filed after an order for reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 1.501 submission is filed after the date of an order for reexamination, the submission will be stored until the reexamination is concluded and will not be considered by the examiner during the reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note 37 CFR 1.502 and 1.902. After reexamination concludes, the submission will be entered in the patent file. The patent owner and third-party submitter (if known) should be notified by letter that the submission was stored; third-party requester should also receive a copy of the notification letter pursuant to 37 CFR 1.550(f).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria for third-party submissions (prior to reexamination order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the 1.501 submission is proper prior to an order in any pending reexamination, it should be entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper means limited to allowed materials (patents/printed pubs/owner statements), includes requisite citation description, information, and proof of service on the patent owner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry criteria for third-party submissions (after reexamination order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a 1.501 submission is filed after an order for reexamination, it must include proof of service on the patent owner to be deemed proper and will be stored until conclusion of the reexamination proceeding and then entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Absent proof of service the submission will not be entered and will be handled according to non-entry procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission filed by patent owner should be entered
rubrics_metrics.description: If a proper 37 CFR 1.501 submission is filed by the patent owner, it should be entered in the file whether filed prior to or after an order for reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No notification to the patent owner is necessary for entry of the owner's proper submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-qualifying submissions – third party
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party 1.501 submission that is not proper (e.g., not limited to patents/printed publications/patent owner statements, or fails to include requisite description, information, or proof of service) will not be entered into the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Handling depends on circumstances: if service included and sender known, the submission may be returned, discarded, or closed and the submitter notified; patent owner should be notified. If service not included and sender known, return/discard/close and notify submitter; patent owner not notified. If service not included and sender unknown, original papers will be discarded and patent owner not notified. If electronic filing, requesters may specify email notification preference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Improper submission by patent owner (pre-reexamination order)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an improper 1.501 submission is filed by the patent owner prior to an order for reexamination, it should not be entered in the file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The patent owner should be notified of the non-entry and the submission should be returned, discarded, or closed. Proper submissions by the patent owner in a reexamination after an order should be entered under 37 CFR 1.555 (ex parte reexamination) or 1.933 (inter partes reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of court decisions and litigation papers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office will accept copies of notices of suits, notices regarding other proceedings involving the patent, and decisions from litigation or other proceedings (including final court decisions, remands, vacaturs, and merits decisions) for placement in the patent file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-merit decisions (motions for venue, new trial dates, sanctions) will not be entered and will be expunged if entered. Court papers that provide a party’s arguments (e.g., memoranda in support of summary judgment) will not be entered; arguments must be submitted via the proper procedural vehicle. The Office may return/expunge/discard overly voluminous submissions; submitters should limit submissions to what is relevant and resubmit. Submissions must be provided without additional comment; highlighting, underlining, fluorescent marking, etc., goes beyond a bare notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public access and handling of non-patent literature (NPL)
rubrics_metrics.description: All reexamination and patent files are open to the public, and reexamination files are scanned into IFW to provide an electronic copy; however, images of NPL cited in public files are not available for viewing or downloading through Patent Center.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certified copies of full contents of the files, including NPL, are available from the Patent and Trademark Copy Fulfillment Branch and may be ordered via the Certified Copy Center storefront.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantial new question of patentability required
rubrics_metrics.description: A reexamination request must present a 'substantial new question of patentability' (35 U.S.C. 303(a)) for reexamination to be ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office initially determines whether such a new question is presented; if so, reexamination will be ordered and proceed with special dispatch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic characteristics of ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Ex parte reexamination characteristics include: (A) anyone can request reexamination at any time during enforceability; (B) under 35 U.S.C. 304, prior art is limited to patents or printed publications applied under 102/103 (but 257 is not limited); (C) a substantial new question of patentability must be present; (D) the proceeding is ex parte in nature; (E) decision on the request must be made no later than 3 months from filing; (F) a reexamination proceeding will normally be conducted to conclusion and issuance of a reexamination certificate; (G) the scope of a claim cannot be enlarged by amendment; (H) files are open to the public (subject to noted exceptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are procedural constraints and expectations for conducting ex parte reexamination, e.g., timeframes ('special dispatch') and limitations on allowable rejections and amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(1) — statement of substantial new questions
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for ex parte reexamination must include 'a statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the core threshold showing why reexamination is warranted and must be supported by cited prior art references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2) — identification of every claim and detailed explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must include an identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested, and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each patent owner statement relied upon under § 1.501(a)(2), the request must explain how that statement is used to determine claim meaning and how each relevant claim is interpreted. The requester may, if appropriate, point out how claims distinguish over cited prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(3) — copies of relied-upon patents/printed publications and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include a copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to, accompanied by an English language translation of necessary and pertinent parts of any non-English language patents or publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All cited prior art must be provided in accessible form so the Office can evaluate the references.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(4) — copy of the entire patent and format requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A request must include a copy of the entire patent (front face, drawings, specification/claims in double column format) for which reexamination is requested, and a copy of any disclaimer, certificate of correction, or reexamination certificate issued in the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All copies must have each page plainly written on only one side of a sheet of paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(5) — certification of service on patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: A request filed by a person other than the patent owner must include a certification that a copy of the request has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The name and address of the party served must be indicated. If service was not possible, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: 37 CFR 1.510(b)(6) — certification regarding estoppel provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification by the third-party requester that the statutory estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 35 U.S.C. 325(e)(1) do not prohibit the requester from filing the ex parte reexamination request is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures that filing is not barred by prior IPR/post-grant-review estoppel; requester must affirm this fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date, fees, and incomplete request handling
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the request is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements of 37 CFR 1.510. The appropriate fee under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) or (c)(2) must accompany the request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the request does not include the fee or meet all requirements, the requester will generally be notified and given an opportunity to complete the request within a specified time. Failure will result in the request not being granted a filing date and may result in placement of the request in the patent file as a citation if it complies with § 1.501.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file a request for ex parte reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person, at any time during the period of enforceability of a patent, may file a request for ex parte reexamination on the basis of prior art patents or printed publications, unless prohibited by the estoppel provisions of AIA 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 35 U.S.C. 325(e)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corporations and governmental entities are included within 'any person.' The patent owner may ask for reexamination but is limited to ex parte consideration of patents/printed publications; for broader issues patent owner may file a reissue or pursue supplemental examination. The Director may initiate reexamination under 37 CFR 1.520.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representative requirements for requesters and patent owners
rubrics_metrics.description: If an attorney or agent files a request identifying another party, the attorney/agent must have a power of attorney from that party or be acting in a representative capacity under § 1.34. A patent owner may not be represented in reexamination by anyone not registered to practice before the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In order to act under § 1.34, an attorney/agent must set forth registration number, name, and signature. Proof of authority may be required. All correspondence for a requester not the patent owner is addressed to the requester's representative unless indicated otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrictions on examiner communications and third-party inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners should not discuss or answer inquiries from third parties (non-patent owners) about specific reexamination proceedings; such parties should be referred to Technology Center Quality Assurance or Central Reexamination Unit supervisory specialists. Only strictly procedural matters (not directed to any specific reexamination proceeding) may be discussed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employees who conducted a concluded reexamination should not discuss whether a certain reference was considered or whether a claim would have been allowed. Patent practitioners must not make improper inquiries of examiners (see 37 CFR 11.804).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of submissions not permitted entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Any submission that is not permitted entry will be returned, expunged, or discarded at the sole discretion of the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If volume of papers from litigation is too lengthy, the Office may return/expunge/discard all or part; a party may limit submissions and resubmit. Submissions must be limited to notification and not include further arguments or information.
